messages:
pagerduty-bot: PAGER — Sev2: elevated 5xx rate across production in us-west-2 (support tier). paging oncall infra-sre.

Alex Chen: seeing a big spike in 504s from the edge -> app ELB. alerts for 5xx and ELB unhealthy targets. dashboards show request latency up across all AZs in us-west-2.

Priya Patel: confirmed from Synthetics — majority of checks failing with timeout ~30s, not consistent with app CPU.

Miguel Ortiz: logs from ELB: target deregistering then re-registering, healthchecks flipping to unhealthy then healthy repeatedly. backend instances still report app healthy. suspect network/ENI flapping.

Alex Chen: running quick curl to service from a jumpbox in us-west-2: 
```
curl -sv https://api.redwood.ai/health --max-time 10
* Connected to alb-usw2.example.net port 443 (#0)
* SSL connection ok
> GET /health HTTP/1.1
< HTTP/1.1 504 Gateway Time-out
* Connection #0 to host alb-usw2.example.net left intact
```

Dana Li: traceroute from two AZs shows hop to ENI/eni-xxxxx timing out in az-b and az-c but az-a path mostly okay. packet drops mid-path.

infra-sre: stack metrics show ENI transmit errors rising on some hypervisors. also seeing Route53 health checks for weighted/latency records returning inconsistent results — latency-based routing seems to be oscillating between endpoints.

Priya Patel: customer impact: API error rate ~12% for the last 15m, highest on region-specific endpoints. Some customers on dedicated capacity hitting fail-open logic and receiving degraded responses. send comms?

Alex Chen: yes, post an incident banner and customers email. short message: partial regional network degradation in us-west-2, we are mitigating.

miguel Ortiz: AWS status page shows a networking disruption event in us-west-2 (networking fabric). opened support case 123456789 — escalation to network team. aws-support-bot: Your case 123456789 is now with AWS Networking.

infra-sre: mitigation plan options: 1) force Route53 failover to us-east with low TTL (manual change) 2) shift traffic via global proxy/routing (if we can update edge rules) 3) scale out cross-region instances and warm up new capacity (risk: stateful replicas lag) 4) let AWS fix fabric (unknown ETA).

Priya Patel: quick note — our database replicas across regions have ~20s lag under current load. failing all traffic to us-east might cause some read-after-write anomalies for customers expecting strong locality. need to weigh risk.

Alex Chen: let's do a mixed approach: route non-customer-facing background jobs to us-east first, reduce DNS TTL to 30s, then failover a small percentage (10%) of traffic using Route53 weighted policy to us-east and watch errors. fallback immediately if errors rise.

Dana Li: lowering TTL now on latency-based records to 30s. doing a dry-run weight change to 10% to us-east. will watch ELB/edge errors.

infra-sre: command snippet used: 
```
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z123 --change-batch '{"Changes":[{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"api.redwood.ai","Type":"A","SetIdentifier":"us-east-1","Weight":90,"Region":"us-east-1","TTL":30}}]}'
```

Alex Chen: note: we also enabled cross-zone load-balancing on USW2 ALBs where it was off to try to even out AZ impact. doing instance drains/replace on the hosts with ENI errors to force them onto healthy hypervisors.

Miguel Ortiz: AWS responded: "We are seeing packet drops on subset of ENIs due to a regional network control-plane issue; remediation in progress. We recommend routing traffic away from affected AZs or regionally failing over. ETA unknown." — aws-support-bot.

Priya Patel: 10% weight to us-east — request error rate is stable so far, overall 5xx reduced from 12% to 8%. good sign.

Alex Chen: ramp to 30% over next 10 minutes. watch for replica lag issues.

Dana Li: ramped weight to 30%. errors dipped to 6%. memories: DNS propagation is staggered; customers on long-lived connections may still hit old path until reconnect.

infra-sre: additional step: adding traffic steering at edge layer (CDN/Edge) to prefer us-east origin for new connections from impacted geos; preparing runbook changes.

Miguel Ortiz: small problem: an internal critical customer uses pinned region setting — their traffic stays in us-west-2. reached out to SE contact to suggest temporary configuration change.

Priya Patel: sent customer note and disabled region pin for them with their permission; their errors dropped.

Alex Chen: AWS confirms partial control-plane repair in one AZ; ENI errors trending down but still not fully normal. they advise to keep traffic partially diverted while they finish.

infra-sre: plan to keep Route53 weights at 30% to us-east for next 2 hours then assess. will continue instance replacements in affected AZs.

Dana Li: handing off to night oncall: Dana taking incident from Alex at 19:00 PT. updated incident channel with current mitigation steps and AWS case link.

Alex Chen: thanks — I'll write a quick post-incident note template and start drafting customer impact details for the status page.

pagerduty-bot: Handoff noted. On-call changed to Dana Li.

aws-support-bot: Case 123456789 — AWS network team will follow up with post-incident RCA when available.

Dana Li: logging final mitigation actions in the incident tracker. will keep channel updated if AWS changes ETA or if we need full regional failover.

Alex Chen: closing comments: root cause appears to be ENI-level packet loss causing health-check churn and Route53 latency routing oscillation. mitigation succeeded via partial failover + host replacements. Postmortem to include: TTL strategy, pinned-customer handling, and faster cross-region traffic steering runbook. :memo:
